clue.text: University cleaner in most superior European capital

indicators.note: in tells us the university and cleaner pieces sit inside the word for most superior

parts.note: the best is the most superior
a char is a British cleaning woman, short for charwoman

explanation.surface: A university cleaner working in the very finest building of a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (short for charwoman) is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania, so it is an example of a European capital.

clue.text: Cry lustily about onset of rough altercation

indicators.note: about means the word for crying goes round the other letter

parts.note: to bawl is to cry loudly

indicators.note: onset of picks the opening letter of the word rough

explanation.surface: Shouting loudly as a rough argument begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a noisy fight or quarrel, a synonym for an altercation.

clue.text: Charlie, a comparatively mousy employee in bank

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
mousy means timid, so more mousy is shier

explanation.surface: Charlie, a rather timid bank worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier handles money at a bank counter, so is an employee in a bank.

clue.text: As in a leg, a curious absence of pain

indicators.note: curious means strange or odd, so these letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A medical note: as in a leg, a strange lack of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for an inability to feel pain.

clue.text: Flat Robert Louis misses out on, having no advantage

parts.note: flat and even both mean level

indicators.note: misses out means the word on is left out of the author's surname

parts.note: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A famous writer misses out on getting a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens-stevens means equal or level, with neither side ahead.

clue.text: Place set up for male sheep

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters run upwards, backwards; the answer also appears forwards in these two words, a coincidence and not the setter's device

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: A place prepared for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A tup is a ram, an uncastrated male sheep.

clue.text: He explored old towns initially by hired car

parts.note: a cab is a car you hire to take you somewhere

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word towns

explanation.surface: A traveller toured historic towns, arriving first by taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in answer order, with 'by' just joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Venetian navigator who sailed for England and reached North America in 1497, so he is someone who explored.

clue.text: Trickery getting airmen in court

indicators.note: in puts the airmen inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is made up of airmen

explanation.surface: Deceit used to get pilots into a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft can mean cunning or guile, a synonym of trickery.

clue.text: Relish being on top initially in pub game

indicators.note: in puts the picked letters inside the pub and game pieces

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of on and top

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Enjoying being on top in a pub game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' reads as a verb for enjoying; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Botargo is a salted fish roe eaten as a relish or delicacy.

clue.text: Oddly this sign of embarrassment reveals fatigue

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word this

parts.note: redness, blushing, is a sign of embarrassment

explanation.surface: A blush that shows weariness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness is weariness, a synonym of fatigue.

clue.text: Calm a couple of sons united by length of life

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, so two of them give SS
U is a standard abbreviation for united, as in football club names
your age is how long you have lived

explanation.surface: A father soothes his two sons by pointing to the long life they share together.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or ease a feeling, so it is a verb synonym of calm.

clue.text: Eg seafood dish and coffee served in Puerto Rico

indicators.note: served in places the coffee inside the abbreviation, as a drink is served in a cup

parts.note: PR is the postal abbreviation for Puerto Rico
a latte is a milky espresso coffee

explanation.surface: A seafood meal with coffee served on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large serving plate or a meal served on one, as in a seafood platter, so a seafood dish is an example.

clue.text: Prone, possibly, to be retailing pork pies?

definitions.meaning: someone prone is ... flat, face down
pork pies is rhyming slang for lies

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to sell meat pastries for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retailing' here means retelling, not selling; PORK PIES is Cockney rhyming slang for lies (a pork pie is a British cold meat pastry).
explanation.definitionFit: Lying describes a body stretched out flat, and also the act of telling untruths.

clue.text: Protected sheepdog, not one of bright colour

indicators.note: not one means the letter standing for one is dropped from the dog's name

parts.note: a sheltie is a Shetland sheepdog
I is the Roman numeral for one
red is a bright colour

explanation.surface: A sheepdog kept safe, despite not being brightly coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: SHELTIE is the pet name for a Shetland sheepdog; drop I for SHELTE, then add RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered means shielded from harm or weather, a synonym of protected.

clue.text: Like the shriek if this cosmetic procedure goes wrong?

definitions.text: Like the shriek if this cosmetic procedure goes wrong?

parts.words: Like the shriek if this cosmetic procedure goes wrong?
parts.note: the phrase for a very loud shriek is also the name of a cosmetic procedure that would hurt if botched

explanation.walkthrough: A deafening scream is described with the very word for making a hole in an earlobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear-piercing means very shrill, and is also the process of making holes for earrings.

clue.text: Vehicle a motoring organisation brought from east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A breakdown service brings a vehicle back from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British roadside rescue club, like the AA.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle, so the answer is an example of a vehicle.

clue.text: Accountant at fair gets wind up, needing place to eat

parts.note: CA is a Chartered Accountant
a fete is a fair

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: air is moving wind or breeze

explanation.surface: An accountant at a fair gets agitated and needs somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets wind up' means gets anxious in British slang; here 'up' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, so it is a place to eat.

clue.text: African country's one mistake in first auction?

indicators.note: in places the one-and-mistake pieces inside the word for auction

parts.note: a sale is an auction of goods
I is the Roman numeral for one
to err is to make a mistake
first is number one

explanation.surface: A country's first auction ends in an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First auction' looks like one phrase, but 'first' gives its own piece, placed at the end; 'in' puts one and mistake inside the auction word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra Leone is a country on the west coast of Africa; the clue's possessive is just the link 'is'.

clue.text: Young male Yankee offers to trap first of rare beetles

parts.note: a lad is a young male
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to trap means the offers word surrounds the picked letter

parts.note: bids are offers

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word rare

explanation.surface: A young American tries to catch rare beetles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladybirds (ladybugs in America) are small red spotted beetles.

clue.text: Flyer's downfall, circling oil installation ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first part before the word for time
circling means the word for downfall goes round the oil piece

parts.note: your fate can be your doom or downfall
an oil rig is an offshore oil installation
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, doing time

explanation.surface: A pilot's ruin came from circling an oil platform too early.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD for time comes from rhyming slang 'bird lime', a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: The frigatebird is a large tropical seabird, so it is a flyer in the sense of a creature that flies.

clue.text: English friend the writer would put first, in theory

indicators.note: put first means the writer's piece goes before the rest

parts.note: the writer refers to themselves, so 'I would' shortened to I'D
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A writer would put an English friend first, in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in an ideal world, so in theory rather than practice.

clue.text: Second-class American form of transport

parts.note: B denotes second class or second grade
US stands for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: Travelling second class in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a road vehicle carrying passengers, so it is one form of public transport.

clue.text: Concealed mike at Paddington, provoking great annoyance?

parts.note: a bug is a hidden microphone
Paddington is the famous bear from children's books

explanation.surface: A hidden microphone at Paddington station causes irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London rail station and also the marmalade-loving bear of children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a source of persistent irritation or annoyance.

clue.text: One who speculates over blocking specific part of stair?

indicators.note: blocking means the letter for over gets in the way, inside the words around it

parts.note: the is the definite, specific article
a riser is the vertical part of a stair step
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a speculator stuck on part of a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specific' stands for the definite article, as opposed to the indefinite 'a'; 'blocking' puts the cricket letter for over inside the stair phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser forms theories, so someone who speculates is one.

clue.text: Harris's uncle, a twin

definitions.meaning: Uncle ... is the storyteller in Joel Chandler Harris's tales
The twin brother of Romulus, founder of Rome

explanation.definitionFit: Remus names both the fictional narrator of folk tales and the legendary Roman twin.

clue.text: Quick-witted Republican leaving for bay

indicators.note: leaving says the Republican's letter departs from the word for quick-witted

parts.note: bright means clever or quick-witted

explanation.surface: A clever politician quits his party for a coastal spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a long curve in a coastline forming a wide bay, as in the Great Australian Bight.

clue.text: German city individual making all-out effort

definitions.meaning: A city on the Moselle in Germany

explanation.surface: A German city whose resident gives it everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is an ancient Roman city in Germany; a trier is also someone who keeps trying.

clue.text: Spoken part doctor originally played? Something fishy here

indicators.note: spoken says that the word for part is heard rather than written

parts.note: a role is an acting part
MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: originally picks out the opening letter of the word played

explanation.surface: An actor's spoken lines and a doctor's first performance hide a fishy matter.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLE heard gives ROLL; add MO and the opening P of 'played'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet, so a fish snack is literally present.

clue.text: After rise, censure share value

indicators.note: after rise, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke or censure

explanation.surface: After a price rise, a share's value is criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the nominal or face value of a share.

clue.text: Middle-Easterner lives with painter and priest

parts.note: lives here means exists, is
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A man from the Middle East shares a home with an artist and a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Gulf State's leader covered by a Times supplement at first

indicators.note: covered by says the State's letter is wrapped up by the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word supplement
leader takes the opening letter of the word State's

explanation.surface: A Gulf ruler features in a newspaper supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulf State' looks like a single phrase; Gulf is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulf can mean a deep chasm, which is a synonym for an abyss.

clue.text: Hospital doctor injecting point right in centre of back

indicators.note: injecting signals that pieces are pushed inside another word
in centre of shows exactly where they go: the middle of the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A hospital doctor gives an injection into the middle of a patient's back.
explanation.walkthrough: GIST and R go into the middle of RE-AR.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor below consultant.
